coverage.assessment: Several argumentative bridges were cut by the revision. The Ruskin comparison is gone, as are the chemist's objection, the 'new universe with no common scale' conclusion and the 'unmoral force' link. The surviving sentences therefore lack their premises (F1, F3, F4, F5, F7).

Langley, St. Gaudens and the Amiens party are clear. Two references are weak but minor. 'Adams knew nothing about any of them' (p19) now has only radium as its plural antecedent. 'The economies, like the discoveries' lost its setup earlier, in the first draft. The Ruskin residue is treated under F1.
There is no scene dialogue. Langley's repeated disavowals of the new rays remain reported speech attributed to Langley, and the Gibbon phrase is quoted and attributed correctly.
The dates 1620, 1893, 310 and 1901 are correct. The revision drops Adams's qualification that he had felt the Virgin as force only since 1895, and not everywhere even then (F6).

Detached third-person narration is kept. The moment when Adams realizes St. Gaudens matters more than the cathedral is cut, which loses the motive for the Amiens episode (F2). Nothing from ch. 031's dialogue is anticipated.

Core long sentences survive. Cumulative cuts remove much of the self-mocking narrator: the Milky Way image, the elderly person with no need for alarm, the broken professorial necks, and the forty-five years of futile study (F8).

The dynamo/Virgin antithesis holds. Cutting the 'Cross and the cathedral' and 'absolute fiat … as in faith' lines in p4 weakens the bridge from steam/electricity to faith, though the Cross survives in p3 and p7. That loss is a tradeoff. The more substantive interpretive losses are the 'unmoral force' and 1895 qualifications (F5, F6).
All five dependencies survive at both actual endpoints. Chicago (024) is omitted, but the local gloss 'among the dynamos at Chicago' supplies the needed setup.

findings.claim: The revision cuts lines that the first draft kept. These include the elderly person with no need to betray alarm, the Milky Way image, the forty-five years of study 'quite futile', 'Here opened another totally new education', and Langley's doubt about his own sun. The Copernicus/Galileo/Columbus clause also disappears entirely instead of being compressed.
findings.counterevidence: Self-mockery survives in 'Paradise of ignorance', 'historical neck broken' and the blind-man's dog. The Copernicus parallels were optional.

Since no one else showed much concern, an elderly person without other cares had no need to betray alarm.

findings.minimal_repair: If space allows, restore the 'elderly person' sentence and the clause 'Copernicus and Galileo had broken many professorial necks'.
findings.plan_relation: Optional tradeoff; the plan allowed compressing the parallels to one clause.
findings.reader_effect: Each cut is defensible for length. Together they flatten the ironic detachment the voice profile names. They also weaken the echo between 'broken many professorial necks' and 'his historical neck broken', and soften Langley's doubting temperament.
findings.title: Cumulative loss of the narrator's self-mocking asides

strengths: The dynamo paragraph keeps its full periodic climax, from the huge wheel barely murmuring and not waking the baby through to V1's prayer.
Langley's repudiation of the parricidal rays and 'Radium denied its God' stay attributed to Langley, with the gloss on his Science.

The Lucretius line remains paired with Dante's invocation of the Virgin, and 'The Venus of Epicurean philosophy survived in the Virgin of the Schools' still carries the link after the authorized cut of the tercet.
The ending keeps the pen as blind man's dog, 'what is struck out', and the precise Cherbourg departure on January 19, 1901.
summary: The revision meets length and keeps every verbatim anchor, the 1893 Chicago gloss, the 310/Cross analogy, the Lucretius-Dante pairing and the Cherbourg date. Its own cuts remove several hinge sentences. The most serious loss is at Amiens: Ruskin now appears with no introduction, and Gibbon's real respect for the cathedral is gone. Other cuts remove the 'no common scale' conclusion, the chemist's objection that gives the Boston chemist his point, the 'unmoral force' bridge, and Adams's late, qualified sense of the Virgin as force since 1895. Each needs only a short restoration.
